t: The Secretary of the Interior is authorized to acquire by purchase with donated or appropriated funds not to exceed two and one-half acres of land and submerged lands, waters, or interest therein, at Charleston, South Carolina, known generally as the Fleet Landing Site, for purposes of a mainland tour boat facility for access to Fort Sumter National Monument. Property so acquired shall be administered as a part of Fort Sumter National Monument. There are hereby authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary to carry out the purposes of this section.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "donated" funds or buying land from an outside owner brings non-federal parties into a federal decision. Donating money or selling land is not consultation, comment, a hearing, advisory input, or a right to sue. The section only authorizes the Secretary to acquire and administer land and authorizes appropriations, with no rulemaking and no outside-party process.
fable.s: The Secretary of the Interior is authorized to acquire by purchase with donated or appropriated funds not to exceed two and one-half acres of land and submerged lands, waters, or interest therein

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to acquire land and funds for a specific project. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as the public, state/local governments, or experts) before making the decision to acquire the land. The actors involved are solely within the federal government (the Secretary).
qwen_block.s: The Secretary of the Interior is authorized to acquire by purchase with donated or appropriated funds not to exceed two and one-half acres of land and submerged lands, waters, or interest therein, at Charleston, South Carolina, known generally as the Fleet Landing Site, for purposes of a mainland tour boat facility for access to Fort Sumter National Monument.

opus.w: This section only lets the Secretary buy a specific piece of land, adds it to Fort Sumter National Monument, and authorizes funding. A purchase from a landowner, or the use of donated money, is a transaction rather than outside input into the decision. Nothing requires consultation, public comment, hearings, an advisory body, rulemaking or a right to sue.
opus.s: The Secretary of the Interior is authorized to acquire by purchase with donated or appropriated funds not to exceed two and one-half acres of land
opus.b: The tempting reading is that buying land from outside owners, possibly with donated funds, brings non-federal parties into a federal decision. That fails: a purchase or donation is a transaction, not consultation or coordination before a decision. Nothing in the section calls for comment, hearings, advisory bodies, rulemaking or a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to acquire land and administer it as part of a national monument. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, state/local governments, or experts) before the decision to acquire or administer the land is made. The mere fact that the land will be used for public access does not constitute 'participation' in the decision-making process as defined.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of the Interior is authorized to acquire by purchase with donated or appropriated funds not to exceed two and one-half acres of land and submerged lands, waters, or interest therein, at Charleston, South Carolina, known generally as the Fleet Landing Site, for purposes of a mainland tour boat facility for access to Fort Sumter National Monument.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that acquiring land for a "tour boat facility" implies public access and thus public participation. However, the definition of participation requires the government to *consult or coordinate* with outside parties *before* making a decision. This section only authorizes the acquisition and administration of land; it does not mandate any process for consulting with the public, local governments, or other outside entities regarding the decision to acquire or administer the land.
